fact: The star at the very tip of the Big Dipper's handle — the end of the Great Bear's tail.
bio: Alkaid (Eta Ursae Majoris) is a hot blue main-sequence star about 104 light-years away, the last star in the handle of the Big Dipper. Unlike the five central Dipper stars, it does not share their common motion through space — it only happens to lie along the same line.
cultural: Its name comes from an Arabic phrase, 'the leader of the mourners' — in that tradition the Dipper's bowl was a bier and the handle stars a procession of mourning daughters following behind.
